summary: Aggressive Wi‑Fi fast‑roaming timers on controller cause intermittent IKEv2 VPN rekey failures during floor‑to‑floor roaming
description: Issue summary: Multiple employees reported VPN disconnects when walking between floors or across a building in SF and NYC offices. The pattern is consistent with short transient radio handoffs coinciding with VPN IKEv2 rekey negotiation failures. Impact: Affected users temporarily lose corporate VPN flows (SSH, kube API, internal dashboards) for ~10–30s; some clients fail to automatically rekey and require a manual reconnect. Observed behavior: Client logs show rapid BSS transition events, AP controller shows sub‑100ms roam handoffs but UDP flows (IKE/ESP) are not preserved during the handoff window, leading to missing IKEv2 responses and DPD-triggered rekey attempts.
steps_to_reproduce: Reproduce on-site: connect macOS/Windows client to corporate SSID (802.11r enabled) on sf-office first floor.
Initiate an active VPN session (IKEv2) to vpn-gw-1, confirm stable traffic (ping internal gateway, open SSH session).
Walk quickly to second floor stairwell and continue to AP coverage that forces a handoff (~10–30s total movement).
Observe VPN session: intermittent packet loss during handoff; some clients trigger DPD/rekey and drop session requiring manual reconnect.

investigation_notes: 03/10 10:00 - Collected tcpdump on AP uplink and vpn-gw-1 during a user‑reported roam; observed IKEv2 packets from client reach AP but dropped/errors at controller switching phase.

03/10 11:15 - Packet capture summary: 3x IKE_SA_INIT/CREATE_CHILD_SA exchanges started within 5s window; second/followup exchanges never completed when roam happened <50ms before next hop established.
Controller firmware: 2.7.9; vendor release notes show a known issue with aggressive FT timer settings and controller offload that can suppress certain multicast/ARP/UDP flows during BSS transition.
APs configured with low (50ms) FT handoff timer and 'fast-rx-offload' enabled; disablement reproduced improvement in lab.

Hypothesis: Controller's fast roaming optimization is briefly queuing or dropping small UDP control packets (IKEv2) during Aadaptor switch/handshake; the IKEv2 implementation on client/gateway sees this as missing response and triggers DPD/rekey, causing session reset.

Observed scope: ~8–12 unique devices across both offices over 72 hours; mostly macOS Big Sur+ and Windows 11 clients using built‑in IKEv2 client. No evidence of broad infrastructure outage; issue is triggered by active roaming events.
workaround: Temporary mitigations applied 2026-03-11: 1) Increased device IKEv2 DPD/keepalive tolerance on vpn-gw-1 (chars: ikev2.keepalive_timer increased from 3s -> 10s, DPD retry count from 2 -> 5) to avoid immediate teardown during short handoffs. 2) Controller: set FT handoff timer from 50ms -> 200ms and disabled 'fast-rx-offload' on APs in sf-office and nyc-office. 3) Notified desktop support to advise roaming users to avoid stairwell burst movement until full fix. These measures reduced user‑visible disconnects in controlled tests.
resolution: Mitigation applied and monitoring in progress. Next steps: vendor scheduled firmware patch (3.0.0) roll‑out is planned for 2026-03-18 after validation in lab. Post‑patch action items: revert DPD relaxations (roll back to pre‑mitigation timers), re-enable controller optimizations one AP‑group at a time while running roaming stress tests. Owners: network-team (firmware rollout), SRE (vpn parameter rollback/monitoring). This ticket will be updated when firmware is deployed and after a 48‑hour stability window.
